statements.quote: In order to use the Semantic Area method to quantify the different effects of ideation interventions on creativity, we obtained a copy of the dataset from the DesignAID study (Cai et al. 2023).
statements.locator: PDF p. 3, Evaluating Creative Ideation with Semantic Area, first paragraph; markdown line 63.

statements.quote: We also received copies of the evaluations that were run, being both subjective and objective evaluations about innovation, fit, inspiration, and enjoyment/liking of the final artifacts produced.
statements.locator: PDF p. 3, Evaluating Creative Ideation with Semantic Area, second paragraph; markdown line 65.

statements.quote: Before conducting any analysis, we pre-registered a hypothesis on OSF
statements.locator: PDF p. 3, Semantic Area and Mode of Interaction, opening sentence (excerpt ending before superscript footnote 1); markdown line 85.

statements.quote: This directly confirms the hypothesis we originally registered and generates new questions about whether there was any relationship between Semantic Area (input, seen, and/or selected) and the subjective and objective assessments run by Cai, et al. We expand our analysis to look at the interplay between these data.
statements.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, Semantic Area and Mode of Interaction, paragraph split across the page break after Figure 6; markdown lines 107 and 117. Page-break hyphenation in registered is joined.

statements.quote: Another important limitation of the analyses is that we did not get a comprehensive understanding of the creative process as a whole from the dataset we had access to.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8, Limitations and Future Work, third paragraph; markdown line 253.

deposits.license: MIT License (OSF registration metadata; not confirmation of a license for the inaccessible dataset)
deposits.notes: The paper's p. 3 footnote resolves to https://osf.io/km2zq/ (HTTP 200). This is the public secondary-data preregistration 'Generative Idea Diversity and Area of Exploration', registered 2024-01-12, not a participant-data deposit. The registration API https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/km2zq/ returned HTTP 200, public=true, embargoed=false, and has_data=false, has_analytic_code=false, has_materials=false, has_papers=false, has_supplements=false. Its registration_responses field 72-9 states exactly: 'The dataset is not publicly available'. Field 72-14 states exactly: 'At present the data set is held by MIT CCI and only accessible to members.' These are repository statements, not statements printed in the paper. Only the preregistration text is public; 'materials_only' describes that text, not downloadable experimental materials. The content flags refer to accessible participant-linked data, not the narrative description of conditions. https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/km2zq/files/osfstorage/ returned HTTP 200 and zero files. The nodes/km2zq/ and nodes/km2zq/children/ endpoints returned HTTP 404 because this is a registration; the corresponding registrations/km2zq/files/osfstorage/ and registrations/km2zq/children/ endpoints both returned HTTP 200 and zero entries. registrations/km2zq/files/ returned HTTP 200 with one empty osfstorage provider. registrations/km2zq/linked_nodes/ and registrations/km2zq/resources/ each returned HTTP 200 and zero entries. The registered_from relationship identifies private source project yr2we. License confirmed through https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e972/ (HTTP 200); the metadata names MIT Center for Collective Intelligence as copyright holder for 2023.

Source project identified through the registered_from relationship in the paper-linked OSF preregistration km2zq; not a separately printed URL. Its landing page returns HTTP 200 but only the generic OSF application shell. https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/yr2we/ returns HTTP 401 with 'Authentication credentials were not provided.' Access checking stopped at that point: no sign-in, request for access, file-list query, or download from this private project was attempted. An account alone may not suffice; membership/permission is not established. The public registration says the underlying dataset is held by MIT CCI and accessible only to members. This project is associated with the S1 preregistration, but whether it holds any participant data, which studies its files cover, and its file count cannot be confirmed.

notes: The entire 332-line markdown conversion was read, including the references through PDF p. 9; this nine-page paper contains no appendix and no explicit statement offering public data, analysis code, supplementary materials, or data on request. Paper quotations concern data provenance, preregistration, and dataset scope; line wrapping and page-break hyphenation are normalized, and the superscript footnote marker is located separately. The sole URL in the markdown is the OSF DOI; there are no URLs in the form's data_and_code (both fields are empty). The source PDF URL https://computationalcreativity.net/iccc25/papers/iccc25-rick2025how.pdf returned HTTP 200, application/pdf; the publisher homepage, accepted-papers page, and proceedings page each returned HTTP 200. No public participant/output dataset was identified or downloaded, so no data-file rows or columns were inspected. Status is restricted because the linked registration explicitly describes member-only data and its source project requires authentication, despite the preregistration itself being public. No public data were confirmed that would support arm-specific participant means, SDs, SEs, analyzed counts, paired estimates, or diversity measures for S1. The screening form has no final object and therefore no final.open_items to map individually. The ACM page for the original study could not be inspected because of a bot challenge; all four requested repository search APIs were accessible after reducing the Zenodo page size. No files other than forms/data/c894.json were created or changed.
